title: mesh-build plugin: what it does and when to call it
when: the STL is ready and must become a usable OpenFOAM volume mesh
statement: mesh-build is a DSH bundle for volume meshes: routes snappy (hex-dominant, layers, multi-region CHT), cfMesh cartesianMesh, gmsh OCC route D, plus a checkMesh-based quality gate for each region. Three tools: mesh_hints (these cards), mesh_build (scaffold a case from an STL, or build an existing case along a route), mesh_check (after meshing: metrics + gate rc; minVol is passed separately and is absolute).
recipe: start with mesh_hints({query}) — traps and quality-improvement recipes
new case: mesh_build({route:'snappy', scaffold:true, caseDir, stl, scaffoldOptions:{domainMin,domainMax,cellSize,locationInMesh}})
existing case: mesh_build({route:'snappy', scaffold:false, caseDir, np:6})
after the build: mesh_check({caseDir, profile:'project', minVol:<h_min³/6>}) — look for PASS in verdict, not in “it built without errors”
evidence: plugins/mesh-build/index.js: mesh_hints, mesh_build, mesh_check; data/engine.json — routes, steps, profiles; lib/skill.js — the agent instruction
verified by a live run: v13_best → PASS at minVol 1e-16 (fluid 331 792 / 18.71°, solid 243 965 / 26.54°); e2e snappy 19.6 s → PASS 27 424 cells / 41.34°

title: Meshing and delivery without sim-project.json
when: mesh_build/mesh_check/mesh_deliver run in a clean directory without a project profile
statement: mesh-build works without a profile: project:"defaults", cases default to ./cases, the gate profile is project, and if the case has no system/fvSchemes|fvSolution the gate synthesises minimal copies in an overlay (it does not affect the metrics, an advisory says so). mesh_deliver no longer requires tools/deliver/make_delivery.sh: when the project script is absent a packaged copy <bundle>/scripts/deliver/make_delivery.sh is used (+ scripts/qa/mesh_gate.sh, region_layout.py), and the gate writes its overlay to MESH_GATE_CACHE_DIR=<outDir>/.gate. Verified in /tmp: 2584 cells, gate PASS, DELIVERED, 1.8 MB of artefacts.
recipe: mesh_build({route:'snappy', scaffold:true, caseDir:'cases/cube', stl:['…/cube.stl'], scaffoldOptions:{domainMin,domainMax,cells,locationInMesh,minVol}})
mesh_check({caseDir:'cases/cube', minVol:<h_min³/6>, profile:'project'}) — look for the verdict in gate.verdict
mesh_deliver({caseDir:'cases/cube', name:'cube', minVol:<same>}) — the signature path: passport → gate → openfoam_<name>/ + .tar.gz + ansys_<name>/ + .zip
OpenFOAM not in PATH: pass openfoam:'/usr/lib/openfoam/openfoam2512/etc/bashrc' (installation ids live in sim-project.json)
need your own caseRoots/thresholds/layers — create sim-project.json: gate.profiles, caseRoots, foam.installations
evidence: plugins/mesh-build/scripts/deliver/make_delivery.sh and scripts/qa/mesh_gate.sh — packaged copies with QA_ROOT from MESH_GATE_CACHE_DIR
plugins/mesh-build/index.js: withPortable() instead of the requireProject gate
run of 2026-11-26 in /tmp: gate PASS 18.29°, DELIVERED, roundtrip ok

title: Patch roles after meshing: retype, never split, then re-check
when: the mesh is built and a solver needs inlet/outlet/walls instead of one snappy wall patch plus a symmetry domain box
statement: snappy on a scaffolded case leaves the obstacle faces and the domain box in two patches: one `wall` and one `symmetry` (`world`). A solver needs flow roles, so the types are retyped in `constant/<region>/polyMesh/boundary` — a documented post-step (in a regional case `changeDictionary` does not work, exp-006/D-013). Retyping changes the type of an existing patch; it cannot split one patch into inlet+outlet, because faces are not re-grouped. For a split, build face sets (`topoSet`) and `createPatch`, or give the geometry named patches before meshing (generator `fluid_patches.stl`, hint channel-named-patches). After any retype the passport is stale: `mesh_check` must run again before delivery.
recipe: mesh_patch_types({ caseDir, dryRun:true, roles:{ inlet:['world'], outlet:['a1-cube'], walls:['obstacle'] } }) — see the diff first
drop dryRun: the tool writes a .bak, edits only the `type` line inside each patch, and updates handoff.json

refusals are deliberate: a missing patch name lists what exists; one patch in two roles; type empty/cyclic cannot become a flow boundary; cyclic/wedge need manual neighbourPatch or wedge geometry; multi-region needs region
recheck:true re-runs the gate and reports sameAsRecorded — patch types cannot change mesh metrics
mesh_check({ caseDir, minVol }) afterwards: the boundary hash changed, so the old passport is stale and mesh_deliver will refuse it
appendix C of the benchmark protocol uses foamDictionary for the same edit — mesh_patch_types is the tool that does it with a diff and the refusals
evidence: plugins/mesh-build/index.js: mesh_patch_types (roles, dryRun, recheck), handoff roles carry-over
experiments/_scratch/verify-a2.mjs: 18/18 — retype, refusals, multi-region, recheck sameAsRecorded (66 241 cells, 24.2346°)
AGENTS.md §13 / experiments/exp-006: physical patch type is set after meshing by editing boundary

title: mesh_revise: the reaction table is data, the ladder rung is counted from history
when: a solver run produced feedback (y+ overshoot, non-orthogonality, skewness, missing roles, resolution, domain, units, cell budget, STL quality) and the mesh must be rebuilt, not hand-tuned
statement: `mesh_revise` reads a `mesh-feedback/1` document, looks up the category in `data/advice.json`, and applies the NEXT rung of that category's ladder — the rung index is the number of earlier `revision` entries with the same category in `handoff.json`. `apply:false` (default) returns the plan; `apply:true` rebuilds with `mesh_build` (same STL, domain, levels and minVol from the handoff), re-gates, and appends `{attempt, category, changes, verdict}` to history. Two rules are load-bearing: after three consecutive failures of `nonortho`/`skewness` the tool switches the strategy (snappy -> cfmesh, one downgrade per request) instead of repeating parameters; and at the ceiling it returns `{ok:false, escalated:true, options[...]}` instead of another guess.
recipe: mesh_revise({ caseDir, feedback: { schemaVersion: 'mesh-feedback/1', category: 'yplus', expected: { yPlusMax: 1 }, changes: { uRef: 10, lRef: 0.01, nu: 1.5e-5 } } })  // plan
mesh_revise({ caseDir, feedback, apply: true })  // rebuild + gate + history
the yplus rung needs uRef/lRef (uTau) and derives nLayers from the target first layer and the local cell size
evidence: experiments/_scratch/verify-a3.mjs: 21/21 — y+ feedback rebuilt a layered mesh (66 241 -> 122 977 cells, 9 600/9 600 faces extruded) and passed the gate at the lowered layer-scale minVol
pitfalls: snappy judges its own mesh against minVol: a gate minVol sized for the background cells removes every layer (benchmark DEF-10). The yplus rung lowers the snappy threshold to firstLayer^3/6 and the gate threshold with it
layers need room: on a 10 mm cube with a 2 mm gap the medial-axis limit removes the extrusion; the same request on a case with a wider domain grows all 9 600 faces
cfMesh needs system/meshDict in metres before a route downgrade can run

title: A domain that clips the STL still passes the gate — compare the surface with the reference STL
statement: snappyHexMesh keeps only the part of the surface inside the background box and closes the cut with faces on the domain plane; the gate then judges the remaining mesh, so a clipped geometry still reports PASS. mesh_surface_check exports the patch faces from constant/polyMesh and compares bbox, volume, area and an approximate Hausdorff with the reference STL: PASS requires bboxRel and hausdorffRel within tol; area is a diagnostic because a stair-stepped voxel surface legitimately carries more area than the smooth STL.
recipe: mesh_surface_check({ caseDir, stl: ['stl/x.clean.stl'], tol: 0.05 }) after mesh_check PASS, before delivery
bboxRel > tol → the domain clips the geometry: enlarge domainMin/domainMax or pass domain: { type: 'external' }
areaRel large with bboxRel and hausdorffRel small → normal for a snapped voxel surface, no action
pitfalls: surfaceMeshTriangulate is OpenFOAM.org only — the tool exports from polyMesh in JS, so it needs no OpenFOAM
the Hausdorff is approximate (triangle-centroid sampling): it catches clipping and lost features, not micron ripples
evidence: experiments/_scratch/verify-a7.mjs: 12/12 — c2 PASS (bboxRel 0, hausdorffRel 0.0005), sphere r5 PASS with areaRel 0.46, benchmark E1 clipped FAIL bboxRel 0.41
when: after the gate PASS, whenever the STL may not fit the domain (or the domain was derived from the bbox)

title: Probe OpenFOAM capabilities instead of guessing from the version
statement: Distribution-specific dictionary keys are read from the installed build, not from a version table: mesh_capabilities probes the executables and $WM_PROJECT_DIR/etc/caseDicts/annotated, and mesh_build's scaffold writes the probed keys (scale vs convertToMeters, minMedialAxisAngle vs minMedianAxisAngle). On OpenFOAM.com there is no surfaceFeatures and no locationsInMesh; cfMesh exists only in OpenCFD builds.
when: Before choosing a route or a snappyHexMeshDict key, and when a dictionary key is rejected or silently ignored by an unfamiliar build.
recipe: Call mesh_capabilities({ openfoam: "<id or bashrc>" }) — read distribution, version, features and dictKeys
Trust dictKeys: the scaffold, the route steps and the layer key follow them
cfmesh available only when features.cfmesh; otherwise route snappy or gmsh
features.featuresNew decides surfaceFeaturesDict vs surfaceFeatureExtractDict
A patched build is described correctly; a version table would lie — do not hardcode keys
pitfalls: Do not infer the distribution from four-digit vs short version alone: probe the executables
bash rejects `key.snappy.name=$(...)` as an assignment (dots in variable names) — use printf
The probe is cached per bashrc; pass refresh:true after installing another OpenFOAM
evidence: experiments/_scratch/verify-a8.mjs 24/24 (com v2512, com v2606, org 14, route plans, overridden caps)
